propositions: A deterministic shadow comparator must consume observed call/result sets from both legacy and RP-06 projections and detect field-level mismatches, accepting only approved deltas (built-in retune/disable, project DET inclusion, project LLM applicability, positive code-review budget, typed partial-failure, success-only checkpointing).

A repository-policy/contract guard must fail when review gates bypass CriteriaSnapshot to read packaged/project routing directly, when a second discovery scheduler is introduced outside the shared kernel, or when per-unit trace fields enter review/review-status schemas.

The combined default paths across both gates must prove they use one shared policy authority, make no duplicate shadow calls, preserve narrow outputs, survive the real provider boundary, and remain centralized.

A live external-provider canary at tests/external/test_review_discovery_live.py must exercise both defaulted gate paths through real LLM providers (Anthropic, OpenAI, Bedrock), assert narrow final verdicts, and retain reducer-ignored internal journals without printing secrets or raw prompts.

New code must ignore legacy checkpoint envelopes; the retained compatibility projection cannot write new envelopes or issue final verdicts; rollback requires only a code revert to the compatibility projection without journal rewrites or data cleanup.

docs/review-kernel.md must document final ownership (RP-01 owns provider-turn retry, snapshot/execution facts are shared, rollback is code-only), approved deltas, sensitive-data boundary, shadow behavior, and gate strategy boundaries.
